title: Nath Bio-Genes (India) Ltd - 537291 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 19% to INR 4,316 million, but gross margin normalised to 56% from 63% and PAT fell about 8% to INR 384 million.
summary.overview: Nath Bio-Genes reported FY26 revenue of INR 4,316 million (+19% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 525 million (12% margin) and PAT of INR 384 million (9% margin). Gross margin fell to 56% from 63% in FY25 on richer product and market mix, and the tax rate rose to 11% from 5%. Growth was led by maize (volume +54%, value +78%), paddy (volume +25%, value +37%) and cotton Bt, while plant nutrition fell 18% on China export restrictions. Management guided FY27 top-line growth of 15-20% (calling 15% the base case) with slightly higher EBITDA and net margins, though guidance was qualified as conservative.

financial_highlights.change: down about 8% YoY per analyst question; effective tax rate 11% vs 5%
scaled up ahead of FY27 season

segments.name: Cotton (incl. Bt)
segments.commentary: Flagship hybrids Sanket and Jumbo drove Bt cotton volume up 22% YoY, with average Bt realisation up from INR 275 to INR 293 per unit as stated on the call. Management said supply constraints of the prior two years were resolved this year.

segments.name: Paddy
segments.commentary: Paddy volume grew 25% YoY to 75,619 quintals and value rose 37%. Management said paddy growth exceeded its 20-25% expectation.

segments.name: Maize
segments.commentary: Volume rose 54% YoY to 9,639 quintals and value rose 78%; maize is now 10.72% of revenue and the fastest-growing non-cotton, non-paddy crop.

segments.name: Vegetable seeds
segments.commentary: Value fell about 11%, while average realisation rose 6% from INR 1,178 to INR 1,244 per kg, reflecting a shift to premium products.

segments.name: Plant nutrition
segments.commentary: Segment revenue fell 18% due to China export restrictions that disrupted supply; management expects normalisation in the coming year.

segments.name: Cotton-paddy combined and NCP
segments.commentary: Cotton-paddy share of revenue rose to 58% from 52%. Non-cotton, non-paddy (NCP) segment grew only about 4%; wheat and mustard value grew 10-15%.

segments.name: International (Uzbekistan JV)
segments.commentary: JV contributed about INR 15 crore (INR 150 million) to consolidated revenue for the first time in FY26, mainly cotton seed sales.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at 15-20%, with management saying 15% is the expected figure, described as conservative.
EBITDA margin to be maintained, with a slight upward trend in EBITDA and net profit margin in FY27.
Gross margin expected to settle around 53-54% per management's earlier view, versus 56% in FY26.
Finance and scheme-related costs expected to stay at about 1.5 percentage points above FY26 levels as a share of sales, per management.
International revenue target: not more than 10-15% of group revenue over 3-5 years; no financial target set for Uzbekistan yet.
Management said it hopes to cross INR 500 crore of top line soon, with no formal commitment.
capex_capacity: Capex policy is asset-light: only land bank and vehicles are capitalised; management is averse to investing in processing plants and storage, preferring rented capacity.
Cumulative cold storage, warehouse and conditioning godown capacity is 25,000 metric tons.
Maize processing need is about 15-20 days a year, which management cited as the reason not to own processing machinery.
Cotton production constraints of the prior two years were stated to be resolved this year, with production of about 70-80% of target versus 20% earlier.
demand_pricing: India's seed market is about USD 4-4.5 billion, growing at a 12-14% CAGR over five years, per management.
Management said cotton area is flat, so share gains come from competitors, and it expects further share gains next year.
Scheme spend fell to 28% of sales from 32% last year (in value terms, schemes rose); other marketing costs rise with inflation at 5-10%.
Central Asia: management cited a cotton market of about USD 100 million in Uzbekistan and about USD 450 million for all crops; the wider Central Asia market could reach USD 1 billion in 5-6 years.
Management said competition is now in-house, with new products such as product 2020 seen as better than Sanket.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Uzbekistan JV structure, crops sold, and revenue target over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Khurana said the JV has been operating for three years and this was the first year sales matched production; no financial targets are set yet. Dr. Kulkarni said the addressable market is about USD 500 million for Uzbekistan, and management will set targets after the next season.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue will international operations contribute over the next 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said not more than 10-15% of revenue, which at a INR 1,000 crore top line would equal INR 100-150 crore. It described this as conservative.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and revenue guidance by crop, and how is El Nino factored in?
qa_highlights.answer: Top line expected to grow 15-20%, with cotton around 20%, paddy above 20-25% and maize a key driver. Management said El Nino affects crops differently, but it expects balanced growth through crop, geography and duration diversification.

qa_highlights.question: Are there FY27 capex plans for processing, cold storage or new geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex is minimal, limited to land bank and vehicles, because processing and storage can be rented and maize processing is needed for only 15-20 days a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall and tax rate rise to 11% from 5%? What is the effective tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the PAT pressure to higher finance costs, scheme and marketing spend, and gross margin falling from 64% to about 56%. It said PAT margin dips about 1 percentage point, with costs stabilising.

qa_highlights.question: Is cash flow negative and why is inventory rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said free cash flow by formula is about negative INR 13 crore, but cash and bank balances of about INR 70-80 crore offset it. Stock build-up reflects cotton production recovering to 70-80% of target, and inventory is expected to be sold over the next two years given cotton's 5-7 year shelf life.

risks_watch: Gross margin normalisation to 53-56% could continue to compress PAT, which fell about 8% YoY despite 19% revenue growth.
Inventory of INR 4,446 million and trade payables of INR 1,305 million, with cash flow negative by about INR 13 crore on a formula basis; watch inventory turns and working capital.
Finance costs rose to INR 133 million from INR 96 million, linked to working-capital borrowing.
Monsoon and El Nino risk: management says exposure is mitigated by multi-geography and multi-duration products, but no quantified sensitivity was given.
Non-cotton, non-paddy segment grew only about 4%, so reliance on cotton and paddy (58% of revenue) remains high.
Uzbekistan JV has no revenue target yet; international contribution is about 3-4% of revenue (INR 15 crore of INR 4,316 million) and may take time to grow.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and product pipeline, with repeated emphasis on conservative guidance. Cautious and somewhat evasive on margins, cash flow and international targets, which were deferred to next year.
key_quotes: And honestly speaking, this is the first year wherein our product has gone out to a very large scale in different provinces.
So, we expect the top line to be growing between 15 -20% around that time, and I'm again being conservative.
As a matter of policy, as a matter of strategy, Nath has not been investing much in CapEx.
It is always better to under commit and over perform.

growth.why: FY27 top-line growth guided at 15-20% (15% base case, called conservative), with EBITDA and net margins flat to slightly up; backing is management's share-gain expectation and mix (maize, paddy, Bt cotton) with no specific new capacity, and capex is asset-light (only land bank), so support is vague.
